html:
The programme announced on 5 February 1967 in the town of Arusha by Julius Nyerere and his ruling party, the Tanganyika African National Union. It committed Tanzania to Ujamaa, a form of African socialism built on self-reliance.

Ujamaa means "familyhood" in Swahili. Nyerere argued that Africa's villages already lived by sharing and cooperation, and that development should come from farming and hard work, not foreign aid or money.

  • Banks, large firms and plantations were nationalised.
  • A leadership code barred party and state leaders from owning shares, renting out houses or drawing more than one salary.
  • Farmers were to live and work together in Ujamaa villages.

At first moving to villages was voluntary. From 1973 millions were moved, often by force. Food output fell and the economy stalled, though schooling and health care spread. The ruling party quietly dropped the declaration's principles in 1991. It remains a landmark of African attempts to find a path between capitalism and Soviet-style communism.
sum: The programme announced on 5 February 1967 in the town of Arusha by Julius Nyerere and his ruling party, the Tanganyika African National Union. It committed Tanzania to Ujamaa, a form of African socialism built on self-reliance.
